name: Left communism
summary: Left communism is the current of revolutionary Marxism that broke with the Third International over parliamentary action, unions, party-led compromise and alliances. Its Dutch-German strand (Pannekoek, Gorter) holds that workers must rule through their own councils and rejects party leadership, while its Italian strand (Bordiga) holds that a class party must guide the revolution and abstain from elections. Both treat the Soviet economy as capitalist and aim at abolishing wage labour and exchange.
scope: The Communist Left as the defining sources describe it (the Historical Materialism review, Marx200 and the Marxists Internet Archive subject page): the Dutch-German current (Pannekoek, Gorter, the KAPD) and the Italian current (Bordiga, the Lyons Theses, his later party theses), answered from their own texts. Where the strands differ (party, unions) the answer is a documented split. Later groups such as the International Communist Current, whose own platform no defining source ties to the name, and communization theory are not used as sources.
